The figures and data-bearing tables of the manuscript prepared for arXiv version 2
([arXiv:2609.26142](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26142); v2 forthcoming) are regenerated below **directly from the committed result CSVs**, and a numeric audit checks the reported numbers
against them; the Super Learner engine is **not** re-run here. Each figure is
the PDF drawn by [`R/make_figures.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/make_figures.R) (the R scripts in
[`R/figures/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/tree/main/R/figures) and
[`python/paper_figures.py`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/python/paper_figures.py)), shown as a 200-dpi image; the
three schematics (Figures 1, 3 and 4) use no data. The estimator code lives in
[`R/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/tree/main/R); the results it produced are
frozen in [`docs/data/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/tree/main/docs/data). For
the methods themselves, read the paper.

::: {.callout-important}
## Double cross-fitting corrected (October 2026)

The double cross-fit (DC-AIPW, DC-TMLE) released with arXiv version 1 averaged the predictions of both
role assignments, so the propensity and outcome models were not trained on disjoint folds. The engine
now uses one fixed rotation (score fold *v* with *g* fit on fold *v*+1 and *Q* on fold *v*+2, mod 3),
and every double-cross-fit result was rerun with the original fold seeds. The CSVs below carry the
corrected rows; every other row is unchanged. The repository
[`README`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/README.md#correction) lists the main
corrected values.
:::

To reproduce the CSVs from scratch instead (re-running the engine), see the scripts in
[`R/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/tree/main/R), the repository
[`README`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/README.md), and the data sources and computing
environments [at the end of this page](#data-sources).

```{r setup}
## Stage the frozen CSVs in output/, where R/ihdp_contrasts.R reads and writes, and read them from
## there. Nothing below fits a model or touches raw microdata. The figures are the PDFs that
## R/render_page.R drew before rendering (output/figures/), shown as 200-dpi images.
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
invisible(file.copy(list.files("data", full.names = TRUE), "output", overwrite = TRUE))

rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path("output", f), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
kab <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, ...)
fig <- function(name) knitr::include_graphics(file.path("..", "output", "figures", "png", paste0(name, ".png")))
## a numeric table as written by R/make_tables.R, without its title line (the heading gives it)
tab <- function(n) cat(readLines(file.path("..", "output", "tables", sprintf("table%02d.md", n)))[-(1:2)], sep = "\n")
```

# The ten figures and the manuscript's copies {#figures}

[`R/render_page.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/render_page.R) draws the ten figures, then compares each PDF
with the manuscript's copy in [`figures/reference/`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/tree/main/figures/reference)
([`tools/compare_pdf.py`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/tools/compare_pdf.py)): page
count and page boxes, the page structure (content streams byte for byte, and every font and graphics resource
they name), and both files rendered at 144 dpi. A pass needs Arial and the package versions in `renv.lock` and
`requirements.txt`; elsewhere, `--text-only` is a limited fallback that compares the words only.

```{r compare, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(file.path("..", "output", "figures", "compare.txt")), sep = "\n")
```

# Companion diagnostic: IHDP overlap {#ihdp-overlap}

Not a manuscript figure. Step 5 of the manuscript cites it for the IHDP design's overlap: the
estimated-propensity densities of IHDP realization 1, from the seeded diagnostic
`data/positivity_overlap.csv`.

```{r ihdp-overlap, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
library(ggplot2)
po <- rd("positivity_overlap.csv")
ih <- po[grepl("^IHDP", po$dataset), ]
ggplot(ih, aes(pi, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(control = "#B8860B", treated = "#AA3377")) +
  labs(x = "estimated P(A = 1 | X), IHDP realization 1", y = "density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "top")
cat(sprintf("IHDP realization 1: %d treated, %d comparison; scores %.3f to %.3f\n",
            sum(ih$group == "treated"), sum(ih$group == "control"), min(ih$pi), max(ih$pi)))
```

# Repeated splits: how much a single split moves the estimate {#tab-splits}

Behind the *r* = 100 rows of Figures 5 and 6: the single-split estimates of each split-based
route across the 100 splits (`data/nhefs_reps_raw.csv`, `data/rhc_reps_raw.csv`), and the RHC
running medians (`data/rhc_reps_table.csv`; Step 5).

```{r splits}
p  <- rd("nhefs_panel_table.csv")
nr <- rd("nhefs_reps_raw.csv"); rw <- rd("rhc_reps_raw.csv"); rt <- rd("rhc_reps_table.csv")
kab(data.frame(estimator = names(tapply(nr$estimate, nr$method, sd)),
               `NHEFS SD across splits (kg)` = round(tapply(nr$estimate, nr$method, sd), 3),
               check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL))
full2 <- p$estimate[is.na(p$r) & p$estimator %in% c("AIPW (one-step)", "TMLE")]
spans <- tapply(nr$estimate, nr$rep, function(e) diff(range(c(e, full2))))
cat(sprintf("NHEFS six doubly-robust estimates on a single split: median span %.2f kg (IQR %.2f-%.2f)\n",
            median(spans), quantile(spans, .25), quantile(spans, .75)))
settle <- function(s, tol = 0.001) { ok <- abs(s$estimate - s$estimate[s$r == 100]) < tol
  for (k in seq_along(ok)) if (all(ok[k:length(ok)])) return(s$r[k]); NA }
kab(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(rt, rt$method), function(s) { s <- s[order(s$r), ]
  data.frame(estimator = s$method[1], `r = 1` = round(s$estimate[s$r == 1], 4),
             `r = 100` = round(s$estimate[s$r == 100], 4),
             `SD across splits` = round(sd(rw$estimate[rw$method == s$method[1]]), 4),
             `within 0.001 from r =` = settle(s),
             `largest distance from r = 100` = round(max(abs(s$estimate - s$estimate[s$r == 100])), 4),
             `CI width growth (%)` = round(100 * (s$ci_width[s$r == 100] / s$ci_width[s$r == 1] - 1), 1),
             check.names = FALSE) })), row.names = FALSE)
```

# RHC: in-sample vs out-of-fold residuals {#tab-rhc-residuals}

`data/rhc_residual_diagnostic.csv`, from
[`R/rhc_residual_diagnostic.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/rhc_residual_diagnostic.R)
(Step 4): the original seed-1 RHC fits (`real_application.R`), full-sample and five-fold cross-fit, with
the outcome model's residual root-mean-square, the g-computation plug-in, and AIPW's mean weighted
correction. Figure 6 shows the same full-sample fit, but its split-based rows are the first of 100 splits
and the median over them, so the seed-1 cross-fit AIPW here (0.044) differs from Figure 6's DML (0.043).
Without ground truth, the comparison does not establish which estimate is more accurate.

```{r rhc-residuals}
kab(transform(rd("rhc_residual_diagnostic.csv"), resid_rms = round(resid_rms, 3), gcomp = round(gcomp, 4),
              correction = round(correction, 4), aipw = round(aipw, 4)), row.names = FALSE)
```

# IHDP: design, paired contrasts, and the aggregated check {#tab-ihdp-design}

All 50 IHDP realizations share one fixed set of 747 covariate profiles and treatment
assignments; each realization's target is the sample average of its own simulated effect
contrast. The coverage in Figure 7 is therefore conditional on this design, for a sample-average
target. The realizations are generated independently given the design, so the realization is the
Monte Carlo unit. [`R/ihdp_contrasts.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/ihdp_contrasts.R)
recomputes the paired contrasts and the exploratory *r* = 20 check from `data/grade_raw.csv`; the
chunk below runs it and confirms that it reproduces the committed CSVs.

```{r ihdp-contrasts}
gr <- rd("grade_raw.csv"); tr <- tapply(gr$truth, gr$realization, unique)
cat(sprintf("%d realizations x %d fold seeds; sample-average targets %.2f to %.2f\n",
            length(tr), length(unique(gr$seed)), min(tr), max(tr)))
frozen_ct <- rd("ihdp_contrasts.csv"); frozen_pil <- rd("ihdp_aggregated_pilot.csv")
invisible(capture.output(source("../R/ihdp_contrasts.R")))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(rd("ihdp_contrasts.csv"), frozen_ct)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(rd("ihdp_aggregated_pilot.csv"), frozen_pil)))
kab(transform(frozen_ct, difference = round(difference, 4), paired_mcse = round(paired_mcse, 4), t = round(t, 2)))
kab(frozen_pil)
p10 <- function(e) { s <- gr[gr$estimator == e & gr$realization <= 10, ]; tapply(as.numeric(s$covers), s$realization, mean) }
d10 <- p10("AIPW = DML") - p10("AIPW")
cat(sprintf("Small-pilot example (Step 5), realizations 1-10 alone: AIPW->DML coverage gap %.3f (paired MCSE %.3f)\n",
            mean(d10), sd(d10) / sqrt(length(d10))))
cat(sprintf("50/50: 95%% Clopper-Pearson interval %.2f-1.00\n", qbeta(0.025, 50, 1)))
```

# Software reconciliation over 20 seeds {#tab-matched}

`data/nhefs_matched_repeated.csv`: the three implementations built on the paper's Super Learner
library (the hand-coded engine, `tmle`, and `AIPW`), each re-run with 20 seeds and an explicit
0.025 propensity bound. The single runs scatter (SD across seeds about 0.08 kg for a single
five-fold cross-fit), but the medians agree to within 0.01 kg. The combined differences yield
similar medians here; the effects of individual implementation choices are not isolated (Step 7).

```{r matched}
mr <- rd("nhefs_matched_repeated.csv")
cols <- c("hand_DML","AIPW_pkg","tmle_pkg")
kab(data.frame(
  implementation = c("hand-coded engine (DML)", "AIPW package", "tmle package"),
  `median (kg)`  = round(sapply(mr[cols], median, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
  `SD across seeds` = round(sapply(mr[cols], sd, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL))
```

# Supplementary: three-benchmark comparison (not in the manuscript) {#tab-all3}

`data/results_all3.csv`: one run of the full panel on IHDP realization 1, LaLonde/NSW-PSID, and
Twins. Twins is not used in the manuscript and its double-cross-fit rows were not rerun after the
correction, so the table has no double-cross-fit rows for Twins. For LaLonde
the `truth` column holds the \$1,794 experimental estimate, which concerns a different
population; bias and coverage are shown only for IHDP and Twins.

```{r all3}
r3 <- rd("results_all3.csv")
show <- r3[, c("dataset","estimator","nuisance","estimate","ci_lo","ci_hi","bias","covers")]
show$bias[grepl("psid", show$dataset, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA
show$covers[grepl("psid", show$dataset, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- NA
kab(transform(show, estimate = round(estimate, 3), ci_lo = round(ci_lo, 3),
              ci_hi = round(ci_hi, 3), bias = round(bias, 3)), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Numeric audit — every reported number vs. its CSV {#audit}

The deterministic audit
[`R/verify_numbers.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/verify_numbers.R)
re-derives the data-bearing numbers in the manuscript from these same CSVs and diffs each against
the printed value. A table with `0 FAIL` means the paper and the committed results agree.

```{r audit}
invisible(capture.output(source("../R/verify_numbers.R")))
cat(sprintf("%d checks: %d PASS, %d FAIL\n",
            nrow(res), sum(res$status == "PASS"), sum(res$status == "FAIL")))
kab(res)
```

# Data sources and computing environments {#data-sources}

The manuscript's Data and Code availability statements refer to this section and to the repository
[`README`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/README.md#raw-data). Nothing on this page reads
the raw data: they are needed only to refit the analyses, and none of them is redistributed with the manuscript
or here. The source's terms of use apply to each dataset.

| Dataset | Source | Files, under `data/` |
|---|---|---|
| NHEFS (Hernán and Robins, 2020) | the `nhefs` data of the `causaldata` R package (version 0.1.4 on CRAN) | none |
| Right-heart catheterization (Connors et al., 1996) | Vanderbilt's CSV export of the RHC dataset, `rhc.csv`, from the [Right Heart Catheterization Dataset page](https://hbiostat.org/data/repo/rhc) of hbiostat.org (<https://hbiostat.org/data/repo/rhc.csv>). The file analysed is byte-identical to that download (2,320,412 bytes; checked 2026-11-02). The `dr3` loader instead retrieves the R-format export through `Hmisc::getHdata()`, which differs slightly. | `rhc/rhc.csv` |
| LaLonde/NSW–PSID (LaLonde, 1986; Dehejia and Wahba, 1999) | the Dehejia–Wahba experimental sample, `nsw_dw.dta`, and the PSID comparison sample, `psid_controls.dta`, from <https://users.nber.org/~rdehejia/nswdata2.html> | `lalonde_nsw/nsw_dw.dta`, `lalonde_nsw/psid_controls.dta` |
| IHDP semi-synthetic benchmark (Hill, 2011) | realizations 1–50, `ihdp_npci_1.csv` to `ihdp_npci_50.csv`, from <https://github.com/claudiashi57/dragonnet>, folder `dat/ihdp/csv/` at commit `2e51b24788` | `ihdp/ihdp_npci_1.csv` to `ihdp/ihdp_npci_50.csv` |
| Twins (supplementary; Louizos et al., 2017) | `data/Twin_data.csv.gz` from <https://github.com/jsyoon0823/GANITE> at commit `e2997317d5` | `twins/Twin_data.csv.gz` |

[`R/check_data.R`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/R/check_data.R) compares the files with
their MD5 checksums, rows and columns,
[`data/checksums.csv`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/data/checksums.csv):

```{r checksums}
kab(read.csv(file.path("..", "data", "checksums.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
```

| Environment | Used for | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|
| Windows workstation, R 4.5.1 | The original analyses other than the repeated-split and grading jobs; the corrected double-cross-fit run; the figures, this page and the audit | [`renv.lock`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/renv.lock); [`sessionInfo.txt`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/sessionInfo.txt), whose R, platform and package versions are printed below |
| Linux cluster, R 4.4.0 | The repeated-split and grading jobs (`R/nhefs_panel_reps.R`, `R/reps_rhc.R`, `R/grade_ihdp.R`), apart from their double-cross-fit rows | not recorded: the package versions of the cluster's R library were not saved |
| Python 3.10.6 | Figures 3, 4, 9 and 10 and the figure comparison | [`requirements.txt`](https://github.com/ehsanx/dml-alternatives/blob/main/requirements.txt) |

```{r session-info, comment = ""}
si <- readLines(file.path("..", "sessionInfo.txt"))
pk <- grep("^== analysis package versions", si)
cat(c(grep("^R version|^Platform|^Running under", si, value = TRUE), "", si[pk:length(si)]), sep = "\n")
```

**Fits that were not seeded.** The NHEFS propensity-overlap diagnostic (`data/nhefs_overlap_data.csv`) and the
full-sample fits of the IHDP grading (`data/grade_raw.csv`) were not seeded per unit, so a rerun gives slightly
different values; for these fits, the archived files are the reference. Rerunning `R/grade_ihdp.R` for
realization 1 and fold seed 1 on the workstation reproduced both double-cross-fit rows exactly and the other six
rows to within 0.04.

**Refitting.** Refitting a stochastic analysis from the raw data need not reproduce the archived values exactly.
Super Learner fits depend on learner-package versions and on the computing platform, and the rows from the
cluster jobs cannot be guaranteed to regenerate exactly, because that environment's package versions are unknown.
